what_happened: Dispatch fixed file_scope to four files, but criterion 3 (a real numbered verify-deploy gate) mechanically requires editing a fifth: scripts/tests/test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh hardcodes seq 1 20 twice and 21 in its invalid-id list, so adding gate 21 turns a green test red three ways. Plan adds that one exact file with a documented File Scope Note rather than re-widening to a directory entry.

Research report settled every conditional the dispatch left open (path shape, D6 settings.local.json exclusion, the _comment false-positive hazard, the merge.lua identity divergence), so planning needed only to re-derive the corpus figures and make five explicit Decisions rather than reopen any question.

Case 2's bash -c nested-wrapper fixture initially placed '.sh;' with no space, which the lint's .sh-suffix extraction did not match (real corpus always has a space after .sh before any trailing redirect/suppression). Fixed both the fixture (added a space) and the lint itself (extract_invoked_script now strips trailing ;),;,}, characters before testing the .sh suffix), making the extraction more robust to punctuation-adjacent paths.

Phase 6's full verify-deploy.sh battery (no --skip-slow) did not complete within the dispatch's ~45-minute cumulative external-process wait cap. Root cause (confirmed via ps -eo pid,ppid): gate 8's run-all.sh nests a self-invocation of verify-deploy.sh (via a test fixture, e.g. test-deploy-verify-wiring.sh's anti-recursion probe), whose own run-all.sh is forced to JOBS=1 by the nested-invocation guard, making a single top-level invocation take far longer than the ~10 min solo baseline. Not a hang, not a second battery started by this dispatch. Phases 1-5 completed and committed; Phase 6 closed as [PARTIAL] with a full handoff naming the exact resume steps (redeploy, re-walk criterion 3, finish the full-battery confirmation).
